description.narrative:
Overall objective (impact): To support a climate resilient transition towards green partnerships, sustainable growth and decent jobs in Zambia.
The overall objective is expected to be achieved by implementing projects and activities that directly contribute to the fulfillment of three identified outcome level specific objectives (1. to 3.) and expected outputs (1.1. to 3.1):
1. To enhance resilience of ecosystems and improve people's livelihoods based on landscape approaches along the agriculture-forestry-biodiversity-water and climate nexus. 1.1. Enhanced policy and capacity for integrated landscape management. 1.2. Enhanced capacities for watershed management, addressing forest degradation, biodiversity conservation, water resources management and climate resilience in selected target areas. 1.3. Improved capacity for forest policy, governance, management and monitoring systems.
2. To increase participation of smallholder farmers, particularly women and youth, in market integrated environmentally sustainable, resilient, low carbon, circular and nutrition sensitive value chains. 2.1. Improved delivery of transformative services to smallholder farmers, including women and youth.
3. To increase income opportunities and apply sustainable resource management practices for local communities. 3.1. Improved livelihoods through enhanced value chains development in forest products and services as well as diversified income generating activities within game management and protected areas.

Detta EU-initiativ syftar till att främja och investera i rehabilitering och hållbar tillväxt längs den zambiska delen av naturskyddsområdet Kavango-Zambezi genom att (i) öka ekosystemens motståndskraft samt förbättra försörjningsmöjligheterna genom integrerade landskapsmetoder inom nexus av jordbruk-skog-biologisk mångfald-vatten-och klimat; (ii) öka deltagandet av småbrukare, inklusive kvinnor och ungdomar, i marknadsintegrerade miljömässigt hållbara, motståndskraftiga, låga koldioxidutsläpp, cirkulära och näringskänsliga värdekedjor; (iii) öka inkomstmöjligheterna genom tillämpade hållbara resurshanteringsmetoder av lokala samhällen.

This EU initiative intends to promote and invest in the green recovery and sustainable growth along the Zambian part of the Greater Kavango Zambezi trans-frontier conservation area by (i) enhancing resilience of ecosystems and improving livelihoods based on landscape approaches along the agriculture-forestry-biodiversity-water and climate nexus; (ii) increasing participation of smallholder farmers, incl. women and youth farmers, in market integrated environmentally sustainable, resilient, low carbon, circular and nutrition sensitive value chains; (iii) increasing income opportunities through applied sustainable resource management practices by local communities.

The results reported are mainly based on the year 1 report covering the period 1st October, 2023 to 19th December, 2024 and the PTC meeting results presentations attended during 2025. Working in collaboration with several Zambian Government departments and Ministries, the program undertook various activities and attained commendable results. It contributed to accelerating Zambia's ambitions towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, Zambias Vision 2030, the 8th National Development Plan, the National Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement, the EU-Zambia Forest Partnership, and the recently launched Green Growth Strategy.
The following are major results attained:
1. Policy Integration and Governance Strengthening
The Sustainable Landscape through Integrated Management (SLIM) project, which focuses on sustainable land management, successfully embedded Integrated Landscape Management (ILM) principles into key policy reforms, including the National Forest Policy and Rainwater Harvesting Strategy. Collaboration with the EU-funded National Land Audit project improved land governance and mainstreamed advanced spatial data practices. A major achievement from this collaboration was the development of six baseline maps and a flash flood prototype, enabling evidence-based planning for intervention hot spots.
2. Water Security and Climate Adaptation
AWARE 2.0 gained national prominence during the 2024 El Niño-induced drought by contributing to Zambias National Rainwater Harvesting strategy and legislative reviews. The project secured an additional EUR 2.5 million from the German Government to rehabilitate small dams and boreholes, improving water access for drought-affected communities. Partnerships with 10 districts strengthened integrated planning and gender-sensitive climate adaptation measures.
3. Livelihoods and Market Integration
ELSAM targeted 48,581 smallholder households and formed approximately 600 farmer groups, creating a robust knowledge-transfer system. Strategic partnerships with insurers and research organizations resulted in a comprehensive agricultural insurance strategy, enhancing resilience against climate shocks. A baseline survey informed tailored interventions aligned with Zambias Vision 2030 and the 8th National Development Plan.
Unexpected Positive Outcomes
Increased Political Attention: The drought crisis elevated AWARE 2.0s visibility, positioning the programme as a key contributor to national water security strategies. Community Engagement Innovations: Itezhi Tezhi district partnered on water resource management through a 'Cash for Work' initiative, demonstrating strong local ownership. The whole program is implemented through existing local government structures which makes it easy to create synergies with other Government programs such as cash for work for greater results.
Visibility and Advocacy: Participation in the EUs Game Changer Campaign amplified youth voices and climate action stories, strengthening programme outreach.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
